records.response_pred:

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?

Honestly? Not much about the decisions. The decision sequence holds up reasonably well when I look back at it — shelter first, visibility over movement, staying in the search corridor, the mirror panel. The logic was sound.

What I'd change is speed. I told myself I was waiting for the right moment. I think sometimes I was just being cautious when cautious wasn't the right gear.

And I'd sleep more. That's not a philosophical answer but it's true. Fatigue was the variable I kept flagging for everyone else and not adequately accounting for in myself.

records.response_pred:

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. They served no practical purpose.

But I've been thinking about that question for the last few days, actually, and I think I had the wrong frame for it. I kept evaluating everything out here in terms of what it contributed to survival. The flowers didn't contribute to survival. Neither did Michelangelo asking whether we'd remember what home looked like, or DaVinci not being able to get words out when the radio crackled on.

None of that was useful. All of it mattered.

Maybe that's the practical answer, if you need one.
